provenance.construction: Cyclic generalized-bicycle code on the ring x^341 - 1 with a(x) = x^35 + x^41 + x^152 + x^175 + x^176 + x^195 + x^227 + x^335, b(x) = x^24 + x^35 + x^45 + x^122 + x^136 + x^191 + x^192 + x^193 + x^197 + x^218 + x^258 + x^274; H_X = [circ(a) | circ(b)], H_Z = [circ(b)^T | circ(a)^T]. a and b are low-weight codewords of the ideal of a divisor of x^341 - 1 of degree 31, fixing k = 2 deg gcd(a, b, x^m - 1) = 62.
provenance.notes: Designed-divisor construction: the divisor is a product of cyclotomic-coset minimal polynomials over GF(2^ord_2(m)), so its degree and hence k are chosen rather than inherited, and a and b are drawn from its ideal by information-set decoding. Both single-block kernels have dimension 31 exactly, matching deg gcd(a, b, x^m - 1), so neither circulant block is wider than k requires. Distance is a witness-backed upper bound from 24 random information-set seeds at 2,000,000 trials each over 31,061 s, with the per-seed spread running 100 to 104. An orbit fold over every equal-orbit partition bottoms at a validated lift weight of 110, and a single-block circulant search at 10 seeds x 600,000 trials finds nothing under 100. Both witnesses re-verified against these matrices.
